title: In 182 mouse brain regions, similar axonal input and similar cell-type mix both predicted similar spiking phenotypes beyond geometry; the thalamic burst link to cortical input was not wiring-specific
abstract: Question: does the specific axonal wiring of a mouse brain region set its intrinsic spiking phenotype, or do geometry and local cell-type composition explain the same pattern? Data: 62,049 good IBL Brain-Wide Map units in 182 regions (456 sessions, 139 mice, 12 labs), the Knox 2019 connectome, Allen MERFISH cell types and the CCF. Method: each region got an 8-feature spiking phenotype (rate, two autocorrelogram indices, ISI burstiness and memory, spike duration, peak-to-trough ratio, narrow fraction). For 16,471 region pairs we related phenotype similarity to input-fingerprint similarity (F_in) and cell-type composition similarity (T), with controls for distance, a distance-only connectome model and division. The plan was frozen before analysis; inference used 1,000 spatially autocorrelated surrogate phenotype maps. Results: F_in predicted phenotype similarity beyond geometry (partial beta 0.43, surrogate p = 0.001), and so did T (0.42, p = 0.001). In a joint model, T added more unique variance (0.034) than F_in (0.009), in 98 of 100 independent lab halves, but the jackknife interval of the difference just included zero. The distance-only connectome did not beat surrogates. The effect was in waveform shape and firing rate; the autocorrelogram burst index showed no link. In 27 thalamic nuclei, cortical input share predicted burst fraction beyond spatial surrogates (rho 0.74, p = 0.006), but distance from the midline gave the same rho, and S correlated 0.82 with midline distance and 0.90 with the relay cell-type share; S did not add clearly beyond midline distance (partial rho 0.35, p = 0.07). Conclusion: similar inputs go with similar phenotypes beyond geometry, but inputs and cell types are correlated parts of regional identity, and the data do not show that wiring rather than cell type sets the phenotype. Limitations: correlational, region-level, one connectome and one MERFISH brain, approximate isotropic surrogates, extracellular features with pair reliability 0.70.

citations.reason: We reuse its nucleus and unit burst tables and its S definition. We confirm that S predicts thalamic burst fraction beyond spatial surrogates, but we show that midline distance and relay cell-type share predict it equally well.
Its finding that axonal input predicts regional task coding agrees with our finding that input fingerprints predict regional spiking phenotype beyond geometry.
